name: Germany
summary: BtMG makes possession of most drugs a crime, but prosecutors may drop small personal-use cases (§31a). Adults may possess cannabis (KCanG, 2024). The NpSG bans whole NPS groups. Drug checking only where states allow it.

poisonControl.name: Giftnotruf Berlin (other regions: local area code + 19240)

callingForHelp: Ambulance crews (112) are bound by medical confidentiality and usually do not call police for an overdose; police may attend after violence or a death. No Good Samaritan law.
drugChecking: Legal only where a state regulation under §10b BtMG exists, e.g. Berlin (since 2023); several other states have rules or drafts.

npsg.title: New Psychoactive Substances Act (NpSG), as amended 7 January 2026

bmgN2O.title: Federal Ministry of Health: cabinet adopts nitrous oxide and K.O.-drops ban (July 2025)

aerzteblattN2O.title: Deutsches Ärzteblatt: nitrous oxide ban applies from 12 April 2026

hibCannabis.title: Bundestag hib: interim report on the cannabis law evaluation

lsd.note: BtMG Annex I. Possession is a crime (up to 5 years); prosecutors may drop cases involving small amounts for own use (§31a).

mushrooms.note: Psilocybin/psilocin are Annex I; mushrooms, truffles, mycelium and spores intended for intoxication are covered too. Possession is a crime.

dmt.note: DMT is Annex I; ayahuasca and DMT-containing plants intended for use are illegal.

mescaline.note: Mescaline is Annex I. Peyote/San Pedro cacti are legal as ornamentals but illegal if intended for consumption.

dox.note: DOB, DOC and DOM are Annex I, DOI Annex II; other analogues fall under the NpSG phenethylamine group (trade is a crime).

nbomes.note: 25B-, 25C-, 25I- and 25N-NBOMe are Annex I; other NBOMes fall under the NpSG (possession banned, not a crime; trade a crime).

2c-x.note: 2C-B, 2C-C, 2C-D, 2C-E, 2C-I and 2C-P are Annex I; other 2C-x fall under the NpSG phenethylamine group.

2c-t-x.note: 2C-T-2 and 2C-T-7 are Annex I; other 2C-T-x fall under the NpSG (possession banned but not a crime; trade a crime).

5-meo-xxt.note: 5-MeO-DMT and 5-MeO-DiPT are Annex I. 5-MeO-MiPT etc. fall under the NpSG tryptamine group: possession banned (not a crime), trade a crime.

cannabis.note: Adults 18+: 25 g in public, 50 g and 3 plants at home; social clubs, no shops. 25–30 g is a fine, more a crime. No use near schools. Law under evaluation.

ketamine.note: Not under the BtMG; prescription-only medicine (AMVV). Selling it breaches medicines law; possession for own use is not itself a crime.

mxe.note: BtMG Annex I; possession is a crime.

dxm.note: Pharmacy-only cough medicine sold without prescription (not listed in the AMVV); not a controlled drug.

nitrous.note: Since 12 Apr 2026: no sale to or possession by under-18s, no online or vending-machine sales; cartridges max 8.4 g, max 10 per sale; bigger tanks banned.

amphetamines.note: Amphetamine is Annex III, methamphetamine Annex II: possession without prescription is a crime. ADHD drugs need a narcotics prescription.

mdma.note: BtMG Annex I. Possession is a crime (up to 5 years); §31a may apply to small amounts for own use.

cocaine.note: BtMG Annex III. Possession without prescription is a crime (up to 5 years); small personal-use cases may be dropped (§31a).

caffeine.note: Not a controlled substance; sold freely in food, drinks and tablets.

alcohol.note: Beer and wine from 16 (14 with a parent), spirits and alcopops from 18.

ghb/gbl.note: GHB is Annex III (sodium oxybate on prescription). Since 2026, GBL and 1,4-BD (>20%) are NpSG-banned except industrial use; trade is a crime.

opioids.note: Heroin is Annex I (diamorphine only in supervised treatment); morphine, oxycodone and fentanyl need a narcotics prescription.

tramadol.note: Prescription-only medicine (AMVV), not under the BtMG; selling without authorisation is an offence.

benzodiazepines.note: BtMG Annex III; normal-dose tablets are exempt preparations but prescription-only. Designer benzos (e.g. flualprazolam) are Annex II.

maois.note: Moclobemide/tranylcypromine are prescription-only. Harmala alkaloids/Syrian rue are not controlled, but ayahuasca (DMT) is illegal.
